en: An inclined plane like a ramp reduces the force needed to lift a heavy box by increasing the distance over which the force is applied.
Rubbing your hands together quickly converts kinetic energy into thermal energy because friction between your skin resists the motion and generates heat.
Earth's gravity pulls the Moon inward, while the Moon's forward motion keeps it moving sideways, resulting in a continuous curved orbit.
Wrapping a copper wire around an iron nail and connecting it to a battery creates an electromagnet because the electric current generates a magnetic field.
Closing a switch completes an electrical circuit, allowing electrons to flow from the battery through the wires and light up the bulb.
A pencil looks bent in a glass of water because light waves slow down and change direction when moving from air into denser water.
Striking a drum vibrates its stretched skin, pushing nearby air molecules to transmit sound waves to your eardrum.
Heating water in a pot causes convection currents because the hot water at the bottom becomes less dense and rises.
Your body digests the chemical energy in an apple and converts it into kinetic energy so your muscles can move.
Pulling down on a rope threaded through a fixed pulley changes the force's direction, allowing you to lift a heavy bucket upward.
An opaque object like a wooden block blocks light rays from a flashlight, creating a dark shadow on the wall behind it.
Touching a hot metal spoon transfers thermal energy to your hand through conduction because fast-moving metal particles collide with your skin particles.
